To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Self Memory System is a complex system in the mind that consists of a set of active goals (the working self), a data base (autobiographical knowledge), and a set of processes (the episodic memory system) that operate on the data base to produce self-relevant knowledge and to modulate access to it, that the system is neurologically based in the medial temporal lobes and their connections, that the system emerges in the second year of life, and that it is a key

episodic memory is the memory system that underlies the sense of self, that episodic memory has a unique function in the brain and is a unique form of memory in the mind, that it is not a memory for the past per se but rather a memory for the self in relation to the past, and that it has been shaped by evolution to provide a means of navigating in a world that has been created by other selves.
the self and episodic memory are closely intertwined and that the self-memory system (SMS) is an integrated and adaptive system that is essential for human cognition and behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of autobiographical memory in defining the self.
the role of autobiographical memory in self-definition and self-continuity, and the way in which the self influences the accessibility of autobiographical memories.
the role of memory and the brain in the construction, maintenance and change of the self.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
memory and the self are inextricably intertwined and that the SMS offers a useful framework for understanding their relationship.
the self is a complex system that is constructed and reconstructed through autobiographical memory, and that this system is a critical component of the human mind.

the Self Memory System is a plausible and useful model that is supported by a wide range of convergent findings, but that there is still considerable work to be done to establish its precise neuroanatomical and functional properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Self Memory System is a dynamic, self-regulatory system, the function of which is to enable us to make sense of our lives.
the self memory system (SMS) is an active goal directed system that is responsible for the maintenance of the self in time and space and that is the basis for the continuity and unity of the self.
the self is not a thing, but a process, an active system that is continually constructed, maintained and modified by the interaction of the self with autobiographical memory and the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
autobiographical memory is a key part of the human self.
memory and the self are inextricably intertwined.
memory is a central aspect of the self.
